translation_direction: ja → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Japanese electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Render the polite oral 〜でございます narration with gentle Vietnamese storytelling markers (Ấy là…, có lạ không chứ!) rather than modern neutral prose.
decisions.rationale: The story was written for the children’s magazine 赤い鳥 in a narrator’s courteous spoken voice.

decisions.decision: Use ! for Kandata’s laughing しめた and his howled order, although the witness ends them with 。.
decisions.rationale: Period Japanese seldom used ！; Vietnamese full stops would misrepresent shouted speech that the narration explicitly labels as laughing and howling.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Kandata’s howled order had been punctuated with Vietnamese full stops copied from 。, which made it sound calm. Exclamation marks now match the narrated 喚きました.
針の山 had been capitalised núi Kim, readable as a proper name or Sino-Vietnamese 金 (gold). Now núi chông kim at first mention and lowercase núi kim thereafter (2.1, 2.2, 2.5).
しめた rendered as the triumphant “Hay rồi! Hay rồi!” instead of the flat Được rồi; the narrator’s surprise marker ではございませんか restored as có lạ không chứ!, mirroring 2.2.
The closing time sentence now mirrors 1.1 (“chắc hẳn lúc ấy… gần trưa”), restoring the frame symmetry of morning and noon.
後には is temporal; replaced spatial Phía sau with Rồi chỉ còn lại and the faintly comic ngắn ngủn with buông thõng một đoạn ngắn.
〜のでございましょう is conjectural: Ấy là vì became Có lẽ vì; the paragraph again opens with Kandata as its topic.
浅間しく思召された now carries both pity and shame (đáng thương mà cũng thật đáng hổ thẹn); じっと rendered chăm chú.
Removed a misattached simile (cái miệng to như một thằng ngốc) and rephrased as há hốc miệng ra như một thằng ngốc.
Lúc nhúc describes a teeming crowd, not one man; removed.
Smoothed the thread’s descent: một sợi mảnh mai lấp lánh, cứ thế êm êm trôi xuống for するすると.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: Đức Phật Thích Ca / Đức Phật / Ngài
glossary.rationale: Honorific reference matching the narrator’s respectful 御〜になる forms.
Follows the ruby reading かんだた; narration uses gã, fitting a notorious thief.

glossary.source_term: 針の山 / 血の池 / 三途の河 / 極楽
glossary.draft_rendering: núi chông kim, núi kim / ao máu / sông Tam Đồ / cõi Cực Lạc
glossary.rationale: Lowercase núi kim avoids reading Sino-Vietnamese kim as 金 (gold); the first mention specifies chông kim.
A peep-show box viewed through a lens, not ordinary spectacles.

witness_decision: Selected the complete Aozora Bunko transcription (card 92, file 92_14545) of the text in 芥川龍之介全集2 (ちくま文庫, 筑摩書房, 1986; 11th printing 1996), itself based on the 筑摩全集類聚版 collected works (1971). This witness uses modern kanji and kana orthography (新字新仮名). First publication: 赤い鳥, July 1918. Ruby readings are omitted from the canonical text; the external character 「特のへん＋廴＋聿」 is encoded as Unicode 犍.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Vietnamese storyteller markers approximate but cannot reproduce the honorific spoken texture of 〜でございます and 御〜になる; some politeness is carried only by Đức Phật/Ngài.
The dateline keeps the Taishō era form (năm Đại Chính thứ 7) without a Gregorian gloss (1918), which belongs in apparatus rather than the text.

title_review.rationale: 蜘蛛の糸 is literally ‘the spider’s thread’. Sợi tơ nhện is the plain, natural Vietnamese equivalent, matches the recurring body term exactly and reveals nothing about the outcome.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Compared the paradise frame, the view to hell, Kandata’s crimes and spared spider, and the lowering of the thread.
Compared the blood pool, needle mountain, silence, the thread’s descent, the climb, rest, the crowd of climbers, the shout, the snap and the hanging remnant.
Compared the Buddha’s reaction, the judgement on Kandata’s heart, the indifferent lotuses, the noon echo and the dateline.
